PHASE SHIFT KEYING

OBJECTIVES
EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
In this lesson, you are taught a method of signal processing that is similar to frequency shift keying (FSK).
INTRODUCTIONM
The new method is called phase shift keying, PSK for short.
The word "keying" in PSK means the same as in FSK. The keying (turning on and off) of a transmitter for telegraph and teletype.
The difference is that in PSK, the phase of the carrier signal is changed instead of the frequency.
PSK is also an old method of signal processing.
But, using modern digital circuits, it still has many applications and is used just like FSK.
Let's begin the lesson on PHASE SHIFT KEYING (PSK)........................
LESSON MENU
Phase shift keying is a signal processing technique that uses a digital signal to phase modulate an analog carrier signal. k: P1001
DISCUSSION
The digital information signal can be from any source.
PCM, DM, or A/D signals can be used. This includes any sync, start, or stop pulses..ulses.
PCM, DM, or A/D signals can be used. This includes any sync, start, or stop pulses.pulses.
DEFINITION
PCM - Pulse Code Modulation
A/D - Analog to Digital conversion
No matter the source, the digital signals are either HIGH or LOW.H or LOW.
The HIGHs and LOWs of the data signals are used to change the phase of one cycle of an analog carrier signal.
For a LOW, the phase of the cycle is not changed.
For a HIGH, the phase of the cycle is changed by 180 degrees.
What characteristic of the carrier signal is changed in PSK?
FSK, or frequency shift keying, changes the frequency of the carrier signal. PSK changes a different characteristic.
TRY AGAIN!
PSK is a digital signal processing technique. In digital, the exact amplitude of signals is not important, only whether the signals are HIGH or LOW.
TRY AGAIN!
Shown below are two basic phase shifts used in PSK.........
The LOW modulation signal is represented by a 0 degree phase shift.ft.
The HIGH modulation signal is represented by a 180 degree phase shift.ft.
These are not the only phase shift values that can be used...
The LOW modulation signal in this case is represented by a 180 degree phase shift.
The HIGH modulation signal in this case is represented by a 0 degree phase shift.
This table shows some of the phase shifts that are commonly used.
As long as the phase difference between a HIGH and LOW modulation signal is 180 degrees, the PSK system will operate correctly.
If a PSK system uses a phase shift of 90 degrees for a LOW, what is the phase shift for a HIGH?
0 degrees represents a 90 degree phase shift between a HIGH and LOW. PSK systems uses a phase shift difference of 180 degrees..
TRY AGAIN!
180 degrees represents a 90 degree phase shift between a HIGH and LOW. PSK systems use a phase shift difference of 180 degrees.
TRY AGAIN!
The two phase PSK system has one disadvantage. It is SLOW. omputer data over telephone lines.
Remember, there is only one bit of digital data for each cycle of the carrier signal.
Also, the frequency ( or Bit Rate ) of digital data in a computer is higher than the allowed carrier frequencies in telephone systems.
This will slow down the transmission of digital data when telephone lines are used as the transmission medium.
To help overcome the slow speed, a four phase shift system is used instead of a two phase shift system.
The four phase shift system is called quad phase shift keying, QPSK for short.
QPSK is different from PSK in two ways: two bits of data are used to phase shift a cycle of the carrier signal, and the phase is shifted in increments of 90
This doubles the speed of transmission by producing four different phases instead of just two.
This doubles the speed of transmission by producing four different phases instead of just two.
FOUR PHASES - There are four possible combinations that can be achieved by using two binary bits: 00, 01, 10, and 11.
For a 00, the phase of that cycle is not changed.
For a 11, the phase of that cycle is changed by 180 degrees.
For a 01, the phase of that cycle is changed by 90 degrees.
For a 10, the phase of that cycle is changed by 270 degrees.
What are the phase increments in a QPSK system??
Phase increments of 180 degrees allow only two shifts since there are 360 degrees in a cycle. The PSK system uses 180 degree phase shifts.
TRY AGAIN!
Phase increments of 0 degrees allow no shifts. Zero degree increments can not be used in PSK or QPSK systems.
TRY AGAIN!
An important point about QPSK is that the phase shifts for 00 and 11 match the phase shifts in PSK for 0 and 1.
This allows modulator and demodulator circuits to operate in either PSK or QPSK without circuit modifications.
Also, other phase shifts can be used, just as in PSK.......
Last, let's talk about the characteristics of PSK signals..
The carrier frequency actually limits the digital data rate, as you will see.u will see.
The carrier frequency, fc, must be the same frequency or half the frequency of the digital signal's bit rate/frequency, BR.
In PSK, one cycle is used for each bit of information......
In QPSK, one cycle is used for each two bits of information.
However, the carrier frequency is limited by the transmission medium or by the circuits in PSK or QPSK systems.
Therefore, the carrier frequency that can be used in a system limits the digital modulation frequency. Computer data can be generated in the tens of MHz.
In a PSK system, the modulation frequency must be the same as the carrier frequency.
In a QPSK system, the modulation frequency must be twice the carrier frequency.
If the carrier frequency in a PSK system is set to 100 kHz, what frequency must be used for modulating signal?
200 kHz is twice the carrier frequency. In a PSK system, the information or modulating frequency must equal the carrier signal.
TRY AGAIN!
50 kHz is half the carrier frequency. In a PSK system, the information or modulating frequency must equal the carrier signal.
TRY AGAIN!
MODULATING FREQUENCY - In a PSK system, the modulating or information signal frequency must equal the carrier frequency.
If the same carrier frequency, 100 kHz, is used in a QPSK system, what frequency must be used for the modulating signal?
In a QPSK system, the information or modulating frequency must equal twice the carrier signal.........................................
TRY AGAIN!
100 kHz is the carrier frequency. In a QPSK system, the information or modulating frequency must equal twice the carrier signal.
TRY AGAIN!
MODULATING FREQUENCY - In a QPSK system, the modulating or information signal frequency must equal twice the carrier frequency.
The next characteristic is bandwidth.......................
The bandwidth of a PSK or QPSK system is always the frequency of the carrier signal.
There is no amplitude modulation or frequency modulation to generate sidebands.
Note that phase shifts do produce slight frequency shifts. However, the sidebands that are created are not used in the system.
The next characteristic is noise...........................
Besides quantization noise when converting analog information signals to digital, PSK systems add PHASE noise.
Phase noise is produced by the transmission medium causing phase shifts in the PSK signal. This is not good in a phase dependent system.
For example, if a signal representing 01 is phase shifted 180 degrees by the transmission medium, the demodulated PSK signal is incorrect. The phase shift indicates that noise was introduced...
In the PSK system, where 180 degree phase shifts are used, phase noise is normally not a problem.
The phase shift caused by the transmission medium is usually not large enough to change signals 180 degrees. The demodulator will convert the PSK signal to digital correctly.
In the QPSK system, where 90 degree phase shifts are used, phase noise many be a problem.
The phase shift caused by the transmission medium can be large enough to cause the demodulator to convert the QPSK signal to digital incorrectly.
If a QPSK signal of 00 is phase shifted by 90 by the transmission medium, what is the signal converted to in the demodulator?
A 00 QPSK signal has a 0 degree phase shift. If changed to 90 degrees, the output of the demodulator is not 00 (00 is a 0 degree phase shift).
TRY AGAIN!
A 00 QPSK signal has a 0 degree phase shift. If changed to 90 degrees, the output of the demodulator is not 11 (11 is a 180 degree phase shift).
TRY AGAIN!
The last characteristic is synchronization.................
Synchronization is used to set up the receiver circuits for a 0 degree phase shift or to disable the receiver's output when no data is transmitted.
Recall that phase differences are relative. That is, a 90 degree phase shift can be relative to a starting point of 0
The receiver must start with a predetermined phase to correctly demodulate the phase shifted PSK or QPSK signal.
For example, if the receiver circuits are set up correctly, a 180 degree phase shifted signal produces a HIGH output.
But, if the receiver circuits are set up opposite, a 180 degree phase shifted signal produces a LOW output.
To accomplish synchronization, the PSK system transmits a sync cycle.
The sync cycle is different form any other cycle.
Normally, sync cycles are transmitted before any data is transmitted and when the transmitted data is all 0s for an extended length of time.
This completes the information on PSK SIGNALS.TITLE........
1. Phase shift keying is a signal processing technique that uses digital signals.
2. The PSK signal is a phase modulated analog signal whose phase indicates one digital bit, 0 or 1.
3. The QPSK signal is a phase modulated analog signal whose phase indicates two digital bits, 00, 01, 10, or 11.
4. The carrier signal, which limits the modulation frequency, must be equal to BR in PSK systems and must be equal to 1/2BR in QPSK systems.
5. The bandwidth of a PSK or QPSK system equals the carrier frequency.
6. Phase noise is introduced into PSK systems.............
7. PSK systems require a sync cycle to set the receiver to an initial phase shift.

PSK MODULATOR CIRCUITS
Typical PSK/QPSK modulators use six major IC circuits......
DISCUSSION
The modulator is designed to operate in PSK or QPSK and uses the following phase shifts:
DATA SHIFT DATA SHIFT
The basic operation is to generate a carrier signal, phase shift it, and select the output according to the digital information input.
Of course, timing must be maintained and a synchronization cycle generated.
The carrier signal generator is a VCO circuit that is set to one frequency by an external voltage input.
The carrier signal generator is a VCO circuit that is set to one frequency by an external voltage input.

VCO - A VCO is a voltage controlled oscillator. The oscillator produces an output frequency according to the DC voltage applied. If the DC voltage varies, the output frequency varies, as used in frequency modulation and frequency shift keying systems. If the DC voltage is constant, the output frequency is constant. In other words, a normal oscillator circuit.
DEFINITION
The VCO operates like any VCO, only the voltage input is held constant which produces one frequency, the carrier signal or fc.
One output, a sine wave in this case, is applied to the phase switching network.
The phase switching network, usually RC circuits, splits the input signal into four different phase signals.
The four different phase signals are then applied to the data selector circuit.
A standard data selector chip is used to pick which of the four inputs is routed to the output..
What type of circuit is the carrier signal generator?
The carrier signal generator does not use a phase lock loop circuit.
TRY AGAIN!
PROGRAMFILE
TRY AGAIN!
The carrier signal generator does not use a counter circuit. It produces an analog signal and counters do not perform that function.
Which circuit produces the four different phases used in the PSK/QPSK modulator?
TRY AGAIN!
The carrier signal generator develops fc, the carrier signal. It does not change the phase of the signal.
TRY AGAIN!
The data selector picks the proper phase signal for the type of digital data that is applied. It does not change the phase of fc.
Looking closer at the data selector, the input (X0 to X3) that is routed to the output (X) is controlled by the B and A inputs.
If B and A are 00, the X0 input is connected to the output. A 00 input is binary for a 0 or X0.
The X0 input is a 0 degree phase shifted signal. The output 0 represents 0 for a PSK system and 00 for a QPSK system.
If B and A are 11, the X3 input is connected to the output. A 11 input is binary for a 3 or X3.
The X3 input is a 180 degree phase shifted signal. The output represents 1 for a PSK system and 11 for a QPSK system.
If B and A are 01, the X1 input is connected to the output. A 01 input is binary for a 1 or X1.
The X1 input is a 90 degree phase shifted signal. The output represents a 01 for a QPSK system.
If B and A are 10, the X2 input is connected to the output. A 10 input is binary for a 2 or X2.
The X2 input is a 270 degree phase shifted signal. The output represents a 10 for a QPSK system.
If the B and A inputs are HIGH to the data selector, which phase signal input is connected to the output?
TRY AGAIN!
A 0 degree phase output of the data selector occurs when the B and A inputs are low, or 00.
TRY AGAIN!
A 90 degree phase output of the data selector occurs when B is HIGH and A is LOW, or 01.
As you have seen, the operation of the PSK and QPSK modulator to this point is simple. The only things left are the timing and how PSK and QPSK work automatically.
Basically, the digital information is routed through the sync cycle generator to the control register.
The control register holds the data and uses the Q1 and Q0 outputs to operate the data selector circuit as you have seen.
The operation is as follows: The timing block receives fc from the carrier signal generator and outputs three signals.
One signal, at fc, is used to synchronize the data source. Remember, the frequency of the input data must be at fc or 2fc.
Two signals, at fc and 2fc, are applied to the control register.
Looking closer at the register, the data is clocked into the register at 2fc.
Also, the data is loaded to the Q outputs at the fc rate, half the clock rate.
If the digital information signal is at the fc rate, PSK, one bit will be loaded into the register twice.
For example, if the data bit is 0, it will be present on the D input of the register for one cycle of fc.
During the one cycle, the register is clocked twice (at 2fc). The bits 00 are clocked into the register.
The LOAD input now enables the Q1 and Q0 outputs, which places the A and B inputs to the data selector at 00.
With the B and A inputs at 00, the 0 degree phase shift signal is selected, as it should be for a 0 PSK data input.
With a digital input of 1, two ones are clocked in making the Q outputs 11.
The B and A inputs to the data selector are now 11 which selects the 180 degree phase output signal, as it should be for a 1 PSK data input.
When frequency of the digital data input signal is at the carrier frequency, only 00 or 11 is clocked into the register.
This produces only a 0 or 180 degree phase shift. The system operates in PSK..
What are the B and A inputs to the data selector if the digital information is a 1 at the fc rates?
TRY AGAIN!
When the data is at the fc rate, it will be clocked into the register twice due to CLOCK being at 2fc. A "1" input to the register will not produce a 00 output.
TRY AGAIN!
When the data is at the fc rate, it will be clocked into the register twice due to CLOCK being at 2fc. A "1" input to the register does not produce a 01 output.
If the digital information signal is at the 2fc rate, QPSK, two bits will be loaded into the register.
Remember, the QPSK signal is twice fc. The digital information signal and clock are at the same rate.
If the digital information is 00, 00 is loaded into the register making Q0 and Q1 00.
With the A and B inputs at 00, the 0 degree phase shift signal is selected. As it should be for a 00 QPSK data input.
If the digital input is 11, 11 is loaded into the register making Q0 and Q1 11.
With the A and B inputs at 11, the 180 degree phase shift signal is selected. As it should be for a 11 QPSK data input.
If the digital input is 01, 01 is loaded into the register making Q0 and Q1 01.
With the A and B inputs at 01, the 90 degree phase shift signal is selected. As it should be for a 01 QPSK data input.
If the digital input is 10, 10 is loaded into the register making Q0 and Q1 10.
With the B and A inputs at 10, the 270 degree phase shift signal is selected. As it should be for a 10 QPSK data input.
The system operates correctly for either PSK or QPSK signals. Remember, it is the fc and 2fc timing inputs to the register that allow automatic operation.
What are the B and A inputs to the data selector if the digital information is a 01 at the 2fc rate?
When the data is at the 2fc rate, the bits are clocked into the register in groups of two. A "01" input does not produce a "00" output.
TRY AGAIN!
When the data is at the 2fc rate, the bits are clocked into the register in groups of two. A "01" input does not produce a "11" output.
TRY AGAIN!
The last area to discuss is the generation of the sync cycle.
The sync cycle generator preforms two functions.
First, if digital information is being applied, the sync cycle generator passes the data to the control register.
Second, if no digital information is being applied, the sync cycle generator produces a sync cycle.
The sync cycle replaces the data..ation data.
For the system that you will use in the experiments, a sync cycle is generated after 16 zero bits are received in a row.
Note that other PSK/QPSK systems may use a different approach...
The sync cycle that is used consists of three cycles of the carrier frequency.
In the first cycle, the sync cycle generator produces a 0 or LOW output to the control register. No phase shift.
The second cycle has two parts. First, the sync cycle generator produces a 0 or LOW output to the control register for 1/2 cycle, no phase shift.
Then during the second 1/2 cycle, the sync cycle generator changes its output to a 1 or HIGH. A 180 degree phase shift.
Finally, during the third cycle, the sync cycle generator produces a 0 or LOW output. No shift.
The three positive half cycles are unique, information input signals do not produce this signal.
In the demodulator, the signal will be easily recognizable.
Which signal is a sync cycle?yped..........................
This signal is 90 degrees phase shifted. It is a data signal for a 01, not a sync cycle.
TRY AGAIN!
This signal is 180 degrees phase shifted. It is a data signal for a 1 or 11, not a sync cycle.
TRY AGAIN!

PSK DEMODULATOR CIRCUITS
PSK/QPSK demodulators use several typical discrete and integrated circuits...
DISCUSSION
The demodulator is designed to operate in PSK or QPSK and uses the following phase shifts, just like the modulator:
DATA SHIFT DATA SHIFT
The basic operation changes the analog signal to digital pulses, shift the digital pulses into a register, and outputs the information.
Also, timing must be maintained and the synchronization cycle recognized.
The first amplifier is used to compensate the PSK/QPSK signal for attenuation and distortion caused by the transmission medium.
The output of amp #1 is applied to a full wave rectifier to generate timing. The output also feeds to amp #2.
The rectifier is used to produce a ripple frequency used as a reference.
The frequency out of the rectifier controls the operation of the PLL circuit.
The constant frequency output of the PLL circuit runs a divide by N counter, which also feeds back into the PLL circuit, a closed loop.
The closed loop circuit and the higher frequencies used (32fc) ensures accurate timing signals out of the divide by N counter on Q2 and Q3.
Note that the timing signals are 2fc and 4fc in the demodulator circuit. This allows automatic operation in PSK and QPSK as you will see.
What is the purpose of amplifier #1?
TRY AGAIN!
The first amplifier does not rectify. Remember, the PSK/QPSK signal may be attenuated or distorted by the transmission medium.
TRY AGAIN!
The first amplifier does not invert the signal. Remember, the PSK/QPSK signal may be attenuated or distorted by the transmission medium.
The second output of amp #1 is applied to amp #2, where the analog phase signals are changed into digital pulses.
Amplifier #2 is designed to operate in cutoff or saturation.
For a 0 degree phase input, 0 or 00, the amplifier produces a HIGH for the positive 1/2 cycle and a LOW for the negative 1/2 cycle.
For a 180 degree phase input, 1 or 11, the amplifier produces a LOW for the negative 1/2 cycle and a HIGH for the positive 1/2 cycle.
For a 270 degree phase input, 10, the amplifier produces a LOW for 1/4 cycle, a HIGH for 1/2 cycle and a LOW for the last 1/4 cycle.
For a 90 degree phase input, 01, the amplifier produces a HIGH for 1/4 cycle, a LOW for 1/2 cycle, and a HIGH for the last 1/4 cycle.
Notice that the second half of the converted phase signal is the correct data.
This is why 4fc is a timing signal. It divides the converted phase signal into four parts.
The last two parts are the correct data for PSK or QPSK signals.

Referring back to the demodulator circuit, the converted PSK/QPSK signal is applied to a register.
The register is clocked at 4fc and loaded at fc from a second counter.
This means that four data bits are clocked in for each cycle of the carrier signal.
The output is taken from Q2 and Q3 and changed to serial. Q0 and Q1 are not used because the data is in the second half of the digital pulses.

The final section of the PSK/QPSK demodulator is the sync cycle detector.
In this type of demodulator, the sync cycle is used to disable the output, not to set up a reference for phase shifts.
The sync cycle detector receives the converted phase signal from amplifier #2.
The analog sync cycle is converted to 0111.
Notice how the three positive half cycles produce 111......
When the output of amplifier number 2 is 0111, the sync cycle detector generates a reset pulse to the counter and to the digital output.
The reset pulse to the counter causes the counter to reset, stopping fc to the LOAD input of the register. With no load input there is no data output.
The reset pulse to the digital data output disables the output. Again, there is no data output.
In other words, when the sync cycle is received, the digital data output is disabled.
What are the binary digits for a sync cycle?
A 0110 is digital information for a 270 degree phase shifted signal.
TRY AGAIN!
A 0011 is digital information for a 180 degree phase shifted signal.
TRY AGAIN!
